title: Sell Mineral Rights in Manor, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Manor, PA
metaDescription: Manor, PA takes its name from an old Penn family land grant in Westmoreland County. See how that deep land history connects to Marcellus rights today.
heroLead: Manor borough takes its name from the old Penn family manors that once covered huge swaths of colonial Pennsylvania, and that deep land history still echoes through today's mineral title work.
intro: Long before Westmoreland County existed as we know it, the Penn family carved this part of Pennsylvania into proprietary manors, tracts reserved for the family itself rather than sold to settlers outright. Manor borough carries that name for a reason, and while the original proprietary claims are long since resolved, the layered, centuries-deep chain of title that grew out of those original land grants is exactly the kind of record we dig through to confirm what a family actually owns today.

sections.heading: Why Old Land-Grant History Still Matters
paragraphs: Tracing mineral ownership on a Manor-area parcel sometimes means following a chain of title back further than a typical Westmoreland County farm, given the area's colonial-era origins. That depth of history doesn't usually change the modern answer, but it does mean the search takes real care.

The old manor lands eventually passed into private ownership through a long series of sales, and by the time modern gas leasing arrived in Westmoreland County, most of that colonial-era history had already settled into clear, recordable title.

sections.heading: Wet-Gas Value in Modern Westmoreland County
paragraphs: Whatever its colonial history, Manor sits inside Westmoreland's active wet-gas Marcellus window today, the same as the rest of the county, and modern development activity is what actually drives current mineral value.

sections.heading: What We Check Before Any Offer
paragraphs: We pull the deed chain as far back as needed to confirm clean title, check for existing leases or units, and look at nearby royalty activity before putting together a range specific to your Manor-area interest.

faqs.question: Does my property's connection to an old Penn manor grant affect my mineral rights today?
faqs.answer: Generally not directly — modern title is what controls ownership, but we do trace the full chain when needed to confirm there are no gaps.

faqs.question: Is Manor borough itself, or the surrounding township, where most mineral value sits?
faqs.answer: Both can carry value; we evaluate the specific parcel rather than assuming based on whether it's inside or outside the borough line.

faqs.question: How far back do you actually go in a title search?
faqs.answer: As far as needed to confirm a clean chain — sometimes decades, occasionally longer for areas with colonial-era origins like this one.

faqs.question: Do old land-grant references ever cause title problems today?
faqs.answer: Occasionally a gap or ambiguity from that era needs to be resolved, but it's uncommon, and we flag it early rather than letting it surface as a surprise at closing.
